Related: P-lean-start, P-operator-digest, P-batch-gates, P-tool-diet, P-soft-upgrade, B-gap-spend.
data.title: Token economy: measure where lead/agent tokens go and cut waste (report protocol, bounded outputs, model routing, cache hygiene)

data.body: WHAT: ask TE-Q1..Q8 of docs/ddflow/decisions/token-spend.md (defaults stated there), record answers as decisions D-TE-*, update the Answers section. WHY: the research (docs/ddflow/research/token-spend.md) found 52% of subagent spend is whole-context cache rewrites after waits over the 5-minute subagent TTL; the TTL setting is a money/behaviour choice for the operator. TEST: every question answered or defaulted on the record.
data.title: DECIDE (lead asks the operator): token-economy questions TE-Q1..TE-Q8 with defaults; record each answer as D-TE-*

data.body: WHAT: a read-only script (python -I safe) over a Claude Code project dir that prints the aggregates of docs/ddflow/research/token-spend.md section 3: weighted units (input 1, read 0.1, 5m write 1.25, 1h write 2, output 5 from the last streamed entry per message id), per agent, rewrites after gaps >=5 min by preceding tool class, carry share by content class. Aggregates only, no transcript text, redacted. REUSE/LINK: B-gap-spend (ledger) and B-am-ingest (the single transcript reader, TE-Q5): this is interim and its parser is replaced by B-am-ingest when it lands; do not add a second reader to ddflow/ proper. HOW TO TEST: fixture transcripts with known sums; unreadable file gives UNAVAILABLE not zero. ACCEPTANCE: on the 2026-10-23 transcripts it matches the research numbers within 2%.
data.title: Interim transcript token report: reproduce the research aggregates (lead vs subagents, cache read/write by TTL, gap rewrites by preceding tool, carry share) from Claude Code transcripts

data.body: WHAT: doctor reports the effective subagent cache TTL (env CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL, settings subagentPromptCacheTtl, ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H, FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M) and warns when subagents run on 5 minutes; setup/dispatch templates emit the env line. WHY: research section 3.3: 100% of subagent cache writes are 5m, 52% of subagent spend is rewrites after waits >5 min; model saving ~50% of subagent spend. Needs Claude Code 2.1.242+ (check version, UNAVAILABLE not pass). TEST: matrix of env/setting combinations, precedence per docs, version too old. FALSIFIER: new subagent transcripts show no ephemeral_1h tokens. Shares ddflow/api/reporting/health.py with LS-worker-mcp-config (hence the need).
data.title: Subagent prompt-cache TTL one hour: doctor check, setup/launch emit CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h

data.body: WHAT: ddflow wait and the driver's poll recipes never block longer than [wait].max_call_seconds (default 240) and return a still-waiting result the agent re-calls; heartbeat rides on it; the driver text stops teaching 'for i in seq; sleep 8..20' loops capped near 570 s. WHY: research 3.3: 583 rewrite events (163 M tokens, 31% of subagent spend) follow claim/heartbeat+sleep loops averaging 11.7 min; ten minutes waited as one call costs ~4x three short calls. Fallback for hosts that cannot use TE-subagent-ttl. TEST: wait with a held file returns at <=240 s with exit 2-style still-waiting; no busy loop; heartbeat renewed.
data.title: Wait and poll calls return within 240 s so a 5-minute cache stays warm; drop 570 s sleep loops from the driver

data.body: WHAT: a rotate hint (doctor/health and the wake brief) when an agent's context passes [session].agent_rotate_tokens (default 250000): finish the item, write the hand-off note into the item's evidence, stop; the lead starts a fresh agent that begins with ddflow brief. Driver delta documents CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW / CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE for agents and the lead. WHY: research 3.3: 12 agents with 300+ calls = 67% of subagent spend, 39 grew over 200 K; model saves ~40% on top of the 1-hour TTL; lead median context 402 K, one compaction at 967 K. TEST: hint fires at the threshold from fixture usage; hand-off note round-trips through ddflow brief. FALSIFIER: rotated lanes need more review rounds or more rework (compare ddflow metrics, 20 items each). Links LS-budget-per-agent (start size) without touching its files.
data.title: Context caps: lane rotation at 250 K with a brief hand-off, auto-compact window for agents and lead, lead compaction at a task boundary

data.body: WHAT: the launch brief ends with a report template (verdict, item ids, outcome per gate, blockers, pointer to evidence/file; at most 6 lines; no tables; repeat wake-ups give only what changed). Driver gets lead habits: no repeated tables, no re-listing, bounded commands, fewer nudges. WHY: research 3.2: subagent reports are 23% of what the lead adds (avg 785 tokens, 226 reports) and 20% of its carry cost; 62% come from agents that reported more than once. Saving small (0.5-1% of total) but slows lead growth. REUSE: P-operator-digest owns the operator-side digest; this is the agent-to-lead side. TEST: brief contains the template within the LS-launch-brief-budget budget; template lint on a fixture report.
data.title: Compact subagent report protocol: fixed template, <=6 lines, details by reference; wake-ups answer the delta; lead habits in the driver deltas

data.body: WHAT: one shared output budget (lines/tokens) applied to ddflow show, list, status, gate status, review and recall when DDFLOW_AGENT is set or --brief is given; truncation always ends with a footer naming the exact full command and the count cut. WHY: research 3.3: subagent tool results are 4.76 M tokens in 12.7 K results; ddflow show/list/status/brief/recall are 21% (1.0 M), review 7%; no single command dominates. Lead: ddflow show/list/status/gate are 30% of its Bash results. Estimated 1-3% of total. Links MTD-next-hints (hints, capped 400 bytes). TEST: golden outputs under and over the cap; footer present; --json unchanged unless asked.
data.title: Bounded outputs: default caps with a 'N more, run X' footer on show/list/status/gate status/review; --brief for agents

data.body: WHAT: first an A/B protocol in the item evidence (same task class, cheaper model vs current, record review rounds, ci failures, rework, units from TE-measure); only if rounds and rework do not rise by more than the price drop, add a per-role model key in the lane launch template (Claude Code subagent model: / CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL). WHY: every transcript is claude-sonnet-5-5, so nothing is measured (research section 2); fix lanes are 56% of subagent spend. Cross-family review rule unchanged. TEST: launch template renders the model; default unchanged.
data.title: Per-role model routing: measure first (A/B on 20 mechanical fix items), then a [lanes] model per role; reviewers and design stay strongest

data.body: WHAT: a contract text the reviewers and authors share: a round returns only new findings with ids; closed findings are not repeated; the author batches fixes per round; round 4 is the stop rule (fifth only on the operator's range). WHY: ddflow metrics: p50 4 rounds, p90 8, max 26 over 1186 items; rubber_duck 57% and critic 55% produce findings; review waits are 11% of subagent spend. LINK: P-batch-gates (BG-review) for line-sized units, D-review-rounds-4. TEST: doc lint plus a fixture review output that repeats a closed finding is flagged by the checker the brief names.
data.title: Review economy: reviewer prompt contract (no repeated closed findings, delta rounds) and a round-4 stop rule in the brief

data.body: WHAT: agents that hit 'monthly spend limit' record a one-line state; ddflow lists the stopped ones and emits one resume text for the lead to broadcast. WHY: research 3.3: 15 subagent runs and 2 lead turns hit the limit; resume rewrites 5.5 M tokens (1% of spend) plus per-agent nudges. Reuse B-quota-pause, do not build a second pause path. TEST: fixture limit message to stopped list to resume text.
data.title: Spend-limit stop and resume: one-line state on the limit message, one command resumes all stopped agents

data.body: WHAT: a help topic and doctor notes: do not change model/effort/MCP set mid-session, keep MCP tools deferred (tool search), set idleCompaction, show the 'Prompt cache (main)' /usage line in the status line; note for P-soft-upgrade that list_changed with deferred tools does not bust the cache. WHY: research 3.2: the lead's only large cache writes were 6 idle expiries (13% of the lead, 0.9% of total); no tool-list change busted it. TEST: help topic exists, parity test passes.
data.title: Cache hygiene for sessions: stable tool list and system prompt, tool search on, idleCompaction on, Prompt cache line in the status line

data.body: WHAT: after LS-worker-mcp-config and LS-lean-profile merge, run TE-measure on fresh worker transcripts and record the median first-call context (research: 52 K median, ddflow part 28.8 K: tools/list 26.8 K, brief 1.4 K, instructions 0.5 K). WHY: start prefix reads plus first write are ~11% of subagent spend, ddflow share ~6%. If above 32 K, file the gap against P-lean-start rather than fixing here. This task links P-lean-start; it does not duplicate it.
data.title: Verify worker start under 32 K after P-lean-start lands (TE-measure); no code unless it misses

data.body: WHAT: dedupe repeated rules text in the brief. WHY NOT NOW: research 3.3: ddflow brief results are 52 K tokens over 44 calls, 1.1% of subagent tool-result tokens; session.brief_max_tokens already caps it. Close with evidence if the re-measure stays under 3%.
data.title: Brief and rules dedupe (low priority): only if post-change measurement shows brief output above 3% of tool-result tokens

data.claim: Subagents are 93% of weighted spend; 52% of subagent spend is whole-context cache rewrites after waits over the 5-minute subagent cache TTL; the lead is 7% so messages are a symptom, not the lever.
data.falsifier: Subagent cache writes would show ephemeral_1h tokens or few big writes after gaps over 5 minutes; or the lead would be the larger share of weighted units.
data.mechanism: Subagent requests use a 5-minute prompt-cache TTL (docs: subagents fall outside the main-conversation bucket); every wait over 5 minutes (review, CI, sleep poll loops capped near 570 s) makes the next call re-write the whole context at 1.25x instead of reading at 0.1x.
data.probe: python3 -I scripts over the lead and 98 subagent transcripts (scratchpad ts/*.py): usage fields, gap analysis, replay simulation
data.probe_output: lead 48.5M units (6.8%), subagents 664M (93.2%); 100% of subagent cache writes ephemeral_5m; 1116 gap rewrites = 277M tokens = 52% of subagent units; replay model within 6% of measured; 1h TTL model -50%
data.question: Where do session tokens go when ddflow is developed with Claude Code (one lead plus ~98 background subagents), and is the lead's 'messages 43.7%' the lever?
